secondary.title: Schaftoside, a functional flavonoid from fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum L.), alleviates depression and cognitive deficits via the microbiome-gut-brain axis in stressed mice.
secondary.abstract: Depression involves dysregulation of central and peripheral networks, with gut microbiota alterations increasingly implicated in pathogenesis. Trigonella foenum-graecum L. (fenugreek), a functional food and medicinal herb, has been used traditionally for neurological disorders, yet its specific neuroprotective constituents remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the antidepressant potential of schaftoside, the predominant flavonoid of fenugreek seed flavonoids, and explored its mechanisms involving the microbiome-gut-brain axis in a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model. Male Kunming mice were subjected to CRS and orally administered schaftoside (20, 50, and 125 mg kg-1) or fluoxetine (10 mg kg-1) for 28 days. Behavioral assessments (tail suspension, forced swim, novel object recognition, and Y-maze) demonstrated that schaftoside dose-dependently ameliorated depressive-like behaviors and cognitive impairments. It attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage and neuroinflammation, restoring hippocampal 5-HT, NE, and ACh levels. Intestinal barrier integrity was improved, evidenced by enhanced tight junction proteins (ZO-1, occludin) and mucin (MUC2) expression, alongside reduced colonic pro-inflammatory cytokines and elevated IL-10. 16S rRNA profiling revealed that schaftoside reshaped gut microbiota composition, notably suppressing stress-enriched Bacteroides and promoting butyrate-producing Butyricicoccus. Untargeted metabolomics identified restoration of tryptophan and α-linolenic acid metabolism pathways. Spearman correlation analysis revealed significant associations between specific gut genera, fecal metabolites, and host inflammatory/neurochemical markers. Hippocampal transcriptomics indicated enrichment of cAMP signaling, dopaminergic, and serotonergic synapse pathways. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from schaftoside-treated donors partially recapitulated the behavioral, anti-inflammatory, and intestinal barrier-protective effects in antibiotic-pretreated recipient mice, accompanied by restoration of the gut microbiota and metabolite profiles. These findings demonstrate that schaftoside, the major flavonoid of fenugreek seeds, exhibits promising antidepressant-like potential through modulation of the microbiome-gut-brain axis, supporting the functional food application of fenugreek-derived flavonoids for stress-related mood disorders.

secondary.title: Temporal regulation of metabolic processes in the marine diazotroph Crocosphaera watsonii WH8501.
secondary.abstract: Marine diazotrophic cyanobacteria play a crucial role in oceanic nitrogen cycling, supporting primary production and ecosystem balance. Crocosphaera watsonii WH8501 exemplifies this capability by temporally separating photosynthesis and diazotrophy. To investigate the regulatory mechanisms underlying this process, we employed mass spectrometry-based proteomics in a high-resolution diel culturing experiment, revealing tightly coordinated protein abundance patterns. Unsupervised clustering of diel protein abundance profiles identified six groups of co-regulated proteins characterized by distinct temporal expression patterns and functional categories. Cluster 1 contained nitrogen fixation and amino acid biosynthesis proteins that peaked at night, while cluster 2 included glycogen metabolism and photosynthetic dark reaction proteins that were most abundant during the night and day-night transition, supporting carbon consumption and energy production. Clusters 3 and 4 were enriched in proteins involved in photosynthesis, cell division, and lipid synthesis, with maximal abundance around midday. Cluster 5 comprised peptide biosynthesis proteins that peaked later in the day and may facilitate nitrogenase complex formation. Cluster 6, expressed during the day-night transition, revealed coordinated nitrogenase assembly, with Fe-S cluster proteins preceding peak nitrogenase iron protein abundance, suggesting a temporally ordered sequence of enzyme maturation. Distinct temporal patterns in iron trafficking to heme and Fe-S cluster biosynthetic systems further indicated tightly regulated allocation of iron to metalloproteins across the diel cycle. Together, these results reveal the intricate temporal coordination that enables Crocosphaera to balance nitrogen fixation and photosynthesis within a single cell and underscore the central role of diel regulation in sustaining these globally important processes.IMPORTANCEMarine diazotrophic cyanobacteria play an essential role in global nitrogen cycling and ocean productivity. In this study, we investigate the temporal regulation of Crocosphaera watsonii metabolism using high-resolution proteomics under diel culturing conditions. Our analysis resolves six distinct clusters of protein abundance patterns across the light/dark cycle, reflecting intricate coordination of nitrogen fixation, photosynthesis, carbon allocation, and iron homeostasis. Notably, we identify temporally ordered assembly of nitrogenase subunits, including precursory expression of Fe-S cluster proteins and indications of tightly controlled iron trafficking systems. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into how unicellular diazotrophs synchronize key metabolic processes under natural diel cycles.

secondary.title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS.
secondary.abstract: MOTIVATION: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. RESULTS: We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. AVAILABILITY: met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

secondary.title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
secondary.abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

secondary.title: Computerized fine motor assessment in Parkinson's Disease: Task-specific measures provide complementary clinical information.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fine motor impairment is a common feature of Parkinson's disease (PD) and contributes substantially to functional disability. Although the Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS Part III) remains the standard clinical tool for motor evaluation, quantitative computerized assessments may provide complementary task-specific information. OBJECTIVES: This cross-sectional case-control study compared fine motor performance measured using the Motorische Leistungs-Serie (MLS) between 19 patients with idiopathic PD and 20 healthy controls and examined associations between MLS-derived parameters and clinical motor severity. METHODS: Motor performance was evaluated using five MLS subtests covering aiming behavior, hand steadiness, precision arm-hand coordination, speed arm-hand, and speed wrist-finger tasks. RESULTS: After adjustment for age, sex, and educational level, patients with PD showed significantly poorer overall fine motor performance, as reflected by the Composite Motor Performance Score, together with significant impairments in selected task-specific measures of aiming performance and visuomotor tracking. Several MLS-derived parameters, particularly aiming duration and hand steadiness, were significantly associated with MDS-UPDRS Part III scores. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that MLS-derived task-specific measures provide objective quantitative information that complements conventional clinical motor assessment in Parkinson's disease. Analysis of individual task-specific parameters may provide complementary clinically relevant information beyond a single global composite score. However, larger prospective studies are required to determine the clinical utility of task-specific computerized fine motor assessment for monitoring disease progression and treatment response.

secondary.title: A contactless approach for accurate sleep stage detection using the Sleepal AI Lamp.
secondary.abstract: Objective.To validate the accuracy and clinical feasibility of a noncontact radar system (Sleepal AI Lamp) for assessing sleep architecture and staging. Although noncontact radar sensors can capture respiratory and motor mechanics without physical attachment, robust validation in large-scale, pathologically diverse cohorts remains scarce.Approach.Nocturnal respiratory and body movement signals were assessed in 1022 adults using simultaneous measurements from a frequency-modulated continuous-wave bedside radar and gold-standard Polysomnography. The cohort included individuals with normal sleep profiles and patients with varying severities of obstructive sleep apnea. A frequency-augmented deep learning architecture interpreted these respiratory and movement signals.Main results.In the independent validation set, binary sleep-wake classification achieved 92.7% accuracy, a Cohen's kappa of 0.792, 96.4% sleep sensitivity, 80.8% sleep specificity, and a macro-averagedF1 score of 0.896. Four-stage classification (Wake, Light, Deep, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep) achieved 77.2% accuracy, a Cohen's kappa of 0.677, a macro-averagedF1 score of 0.768, and balanced accuracy/macro-recall of 77.4%, with stage-specificF1 scores of 0.839, 0.740, 0.691, and 0.802 for Wake, Light, Deep, and REM, respectively.Significance.The findings support the validity of the 60 GHz radar-based system for automated assessment of sleep macrostructure. By capturing stage-specific respiratory and movement phenotypes without physical attachment, this technology may provide an unobtrusive tool for home-based screening, longitudinal recovery tracking, and population-level sleep epidemiology.

secondary.title: Modeling Progressive Brain Volume Losses in Chronic Moderate Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Extensive, but Attenuating.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Progressive brain atrophy has now been widely observed in the chronic stages of moderate-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI), but there is only coarse information regarding its prevalence and magnitude, and whether rate of atrophy accelerates or attenuates across time. We examined these questions in a Canadian inception cohort from the Toronto Rehab TBI Recovery Study. METHODS: N = 123 patients with post-traumatic amnesia ranging from > 1 h to 10 weeks (70%, > 7 days) were administered up to three MRIs at approximately 5 months, 1 year, and 3 years post-injury. N = 32 healthy controls were scanned up to two times on average 14 months apart. Ventricle-to-brain ratio (VBR) was calculated and manual segmentation of the hippocampi (HPC), corpus callosum (CC), and substructures was employed. For each region, annualized rates of progressive atrophy were modeled from approximately 5 months to 1 year and 1 to 3 years post-TBI; proportions of patients with annualized volume losses of 2.5%-5%, 5%-10%, and > 10% were estimated. RESULTS: Mixed-effects longitudinal models estimated robust progressive atrophy in both time windows in all regions compared to controls, but with significant attenuation across windows. In the earlier window, > 10% annualized loss was estimated in 76.2% of patients for VBR, 53.2% for CC, and 25.0% for HPC bilaterally. In the later window, at least 5%-10% annualized loss was estimated in 63.3% of patients for VBR, 49.4% for CC, and 17.7% for right HPC; for left HPC, 6.3% of patients showed at least 2.5%-5% annualized decline. INTERPRETATION: Clinically concerning prevalence and degree of progressive volume losses were observed in the chronic stages of msTBI, with tapering of losses across time, and regional variations. Research is needed to understand and mitigate clinical impact of these declines.

secondary.title: NR-MRC: A No-Reference Magnetic Resonance Curve Estimation Network for Tumor MR Image Quality Assessment and Enhancement.
secondary.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate image quality assessment (IQA) is essential for evaluating tumor magnetic resonance (MR) images in clinical practice and computer-aided diagnosis. However, most existing IQA models are designed for natural images and require reference images for training. Variability in tissue characteristics, lesion location, and lesion morphology, together with the scarcity of high-quality MR reference images, makes quality assessment of tumor MR images particularly challenging. METHODS: To address these challenges, we propose a no-reference magnetic resonance curve estimation network named NR-MRC. First, a magnetic resonance curve estimation module uses nonlinear curve mapping to estimate spatially adjusted intensity and detail features without requiring reference tumor MR images. Second, a multi-scale feature estimation module extracts contextual features at different scales and fuses them with the initial estimates to generate enhanced MR images. Finally, a magnetic resonance scene statistics blind quality model evaluates feature consistency between the original images and their enhanced counterparts. RESULTS: Experiments on publicly available brain tumor and bladder cancer datasets demonstrate that NR-MRC outperforms the compared IQA and image enhancement methods. In the tested U-Net and DeepLab v3 settings, training with images selected by high NR-MRC scores or enhanced by NR-MRC increased segmentation metrics by approximately 20%. These task-specific gains do not by themselves establish improved clinical diagnostic image quality. CONCLUSION: NR-MRC provides no-reference quality assessment and enhancement for tumor MR images and shows potential utility in the evaluated downstream segmentation tasks.

secondary.title: Real-time tracking of vaccinia virus entry using a split luciferase complementation assay.
secondary.abstract: UNLABELLED: A recombinant vaccinia virus (vA4-HiBiT) was constructed with a short, split luciferase HiBiT tag at the C-terminus of the A4 core protein open reading frame. When HeLa or A549 cells stably expressing LgBiT were infected with vA4-HiBiT, the interaction of the split luciferase fragments reconstituted NanoLuc enzyme activity. Upon addition of a membrane-permeable luciferase substrate, a strong luminescence signal indicated core entry into the cytoplasm within 5 min after infection and was proportional to virus multiplicity within the range of 0.5-80 PFU/cell. This direct entry assay was dependent on a functional virus entry-fusion complex, was inhibited by a neutralizing antibody, and was unaffected by an inhibitor of protein synthesis. Entry was enhanced by brief pH 5 treatment of cell-bound virus relative to pH 7 and prevented by pH 3 treatment. Bafilomycin A1, an inhibitor of endosomal acidification, exhibited greater inhibition of entry in A549-LgBiT cells compared to HeLa-LgBiT cells, as did treatment with ammonium chloride, suggesting variations in entry pathways or cell metabolism. Inhibition of entry by latrunculin A and cytochalasin D indicated a role for actin polymerization in both cell lines. Despite the discovery of a conserved furin cleavage consensus sequence in the A16 subunit of the entry-fusion complex, a furin inhibitor did not reduce virus entry unlike results obtained with a human papillomavirus control. These data support the use of this NanoBiT assay for studies of vaccinia virus entry, with application to basic research, antivirals, and neutralizing antibodies. IMPORTANCE: Assays to measure virus entry into cells mostly rely on post-entry events such as gene expression, cytopathic effects, or virus yields. Although fluorescence and electron microscopy can provide direct analyses, such methods are labor intensive and semiquantitative. Here we describe a rapid and quantitative real-time direct entry assay for vaccinia virus with application to basic research, antivirals, and neutralizing antibodies.

secondary.title: Integrating network medicine and foundation models reveals cell-type-specific regulatory alterations in Alzheimer's disease.
secondary.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and neuroinflammation. Although its molecular hallmarks are well documented, cell-type-specific mechanisms driving gene dysregulation remain elusive. While single-cell RNA sequencing resolves cellular states, most studies focus on individual genes rather than coordinated programs. Moreover, a gap persists between interpretable network-based models and artificial intelligence foundation models, which capture complex interactions but lack mechanistic transparency. Whether these approaches converge or provide complementary views remains unclear. We present an integrated study combining SCANet, for reconstructing co-expression and gene regulatory networks, with scGPT foundation model. Applied to over 1.3 million cells across 18 cell types, this approach revealed that Alzheimer-associated transcriptional changes concentrate within coherent co-expression modules, for extracellular matrix organization, immune signaling, and neuronal communication. Genes prioritized by scGPT were largely embedded within SCANet modules, indicating convergence at the gene level; however, higher-order architecture agreement was limited and cell-type-specific. Thus, scGPT highlights influential genes, whereas SCANet resolves their modular organization, providing complementary information. By integrating both methods, we recovered known Alzheimer-related pathways and identified novel regulatory candidates, including the CEBPB-CENPQ axis in vulnerable SST-GABA interneurons. This demonstrates that combining network biology with foundation models enables gene prioritization and mechanistic interpretation.

secondary.title: Reprogramming pathological secretory phenotype of chondrocytes inhibits neurovascular invasion for osteoarthritis treatment.
secondary.abstract: Pain severity in osteoarthritis (OA) often dissociates from the extent of cartilage structural damage, indicating that non-structural mechanisms contribute to symptom persistence. Here, we identify articular chondrocytes as active orchestrators of pathological neurovascular invasion through a pathogenic secretome, rather than merely passive victims of degeneration. Integrated human single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals that OA chondrocytes undergo phenotypic reprogramming characterized by coordinated activation of angiogenic and neurotrophic programs. Functionally, inflammatory chondrocytes directly promote endothelial angiogenesis and sensory axon outgrowth, linking chondrocyte-derived signals to neurovascular invasion and sustained pain. To therapeutically target this upstream mechanism, we engineered MMP-13-responsive celecoxib-loaded hyaluronic acid methacrylate microspheres (HMPC) for disease-adaptive delivery to degenerative cartilage. HMPC suppresses chondrocyte COX-2 activity and remodels the pathological chondrocyte secretome through restoration of miR-339-5p_R-5 and miR-103-3p_R-2, thereby inhibiting angiopoietin-2 (Angpt2)-mediated angiogenesis and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (Bdnf)-driven sensory neurogenesis. In murine OA models, HMPC markedly alleviates pain-related behaviors, reduces neurovascular infiltration, and preserves joint structure. Collectively, this study supports a chondrocyte-centric framework in which reprogrammed chondrocytes govern neurovascular invasion through microRNA-dependent secretome regulation and introduces a smart biomaterial-enabled strategy with disease-modifying potential for OA pain intervention.

secondary.title: Regional brain aging signatures predict mortality through neurovascular immune mechanisms.
secondary.abstract: Brain aging provides an integrative marker of systemic health, but whether regional patterns outperform whole-brain approaches remains unknown. Here, we show that regional brain age signatures achieve superior mortality prediction through identifiable neurovascular-immune mechanisms in 1,240 community-dwelling adults followed for 10 years (120 deaths). While global brain age independently predicts mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.044 per year), a data-driven three-region model combining the left precentral gyrus, left parahippocampal gyrus, and right cerebellum achieves superior discrimination (C-index, 0.81 vs. 0.79, p = 0.032). Integration with plasma proteomics (513 proteins) reveals complement activation and adaptive immune dysregulation as convergent mechanisms. Region-specific vulnerabilities emerge: microvascular dysfunction in the motor cortex, proteostasis failure in the medial temporal structures, and iron dysregulation in the cerebellum. Longitudinal imaging (n = 444) identifies accelerated brain aging phenotypes predicting cognitive decline (HR, 1.558; p = 0.042). These findings establish regional neuroimaging-proteomic integration as a precision strategy linking network-specific vulnerabilities to systemic immune processes.

secondary.title: Open-source hardware platform for automated, non-invasive plant phenotyping through combined RGB and thermal imaging.
secondary.abstract: We present an open-source, modular plant phenotyping platform for non-invasive monitoring of small to medium-sized plants in growth chambers. The system integrates an RGB camera and a FLIR Lepton 3.5 thermal module on an automated two-axis Cartesian gantry capturing overhead images at 24 predefined positions. A key design feature is the use of Hall effect sensors with permanent magnets for discrete position referencing, providing robust, recalibration-free positioning without complex mechanical systems such as lead screws, belt-driven encoders, or step-counting alone. The platform uses 3D-printed components, a Raspberry Pi, stepper motors with rack-and-pinion transmission, and commonly available hardware store materials. Automated image acquisition scheduling increases temporal resolution and eliminates errors from prolonged manual measurements. Companion software enables homography-based projection of RGB segmentation masks onto thermal images and interactive exploration and quantitative analysis of thermographic data. As proof of concept, a multi-day water deficit experiment with soybean plants was conducted. RGB images were segmented using a U-Net deep learning model, and projected leaf area dynamics clearly discriminated between irrigated and drought-stressed plants. Thermal imaging revealed canopy temperature differences consistent with stomatal closure under water deficit.

secondary.title: Childhood peer abuse moderates associations of inflammation and cortisol with subcortical brain volume.
secondary.abstract: Objective: Childhood peer abuse is a developmentally salient form of interpersonal adversity, yet its role in shaping links between peripheral biological stress markers and brain structure remains poorly understood. The present cross-sectional study examined whether retrospectively reported childhood peer verbal and physical abuse moderated associations of systemic inflammatory burden and hair cortisol with subcortical brain volume.Methods: Participants from a community sample completed the Maltreatment and Abuse Chronology of Exposure scale and structural magnetic resonance imaging. Inflammatory burden was indexed by a composite of standardised IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha, and C-reactive protein values (n = 292), and hair cortisol was available in a subsample (n = 172). Bilateral amygdala, hippocampus, putamen, and caudate volumes were extracted from FreeSurfer segmentation. Linear regression models adjusted for gender, age, parental education, and estimated total intracranial volume; false discovery rate correction was applied across the four ROI tests within each marker-by-moderator family.Results: Peer verbal abuse moderated associations of inflammatory burden with bilateral amygdala volume (β = -.095, pFDR = .032) and bilateral putamen volume (β = -.115, pFDR = .017). Peer physical abuse moderated the association between hair cortisol and bilateral amygdala volume (β = .227, pFDR = .035). Caudate models did not survive correction. Core findings remained significant after sensitivity adjustment for broader childhood adversity and current depression/anxiety symptoms.Conclusions: Associations differed across brain regions, biological markers, and peer-abuse subtypes. These findings identify peer adversity as an important interpersonal context for understanding stress-related brain differences.

secondary.title: STEP61 is a regulator of mGluR5 expression.
secondary.abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) is a Gq protein-coupled receptor that modulates both excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission and regulates numerous higher-order neural processes ranging from learning and memory to mood and behavior. Trafficking of mGluR5 to the plasma membrane is critical for its biological functions and phosphorylation is an important regulator of mGluR5 trafficking and function. We previously reported that striatal-enriched protein tyrosine phosphatase 61 (STEP61) interacts with mGluR5 in a proteomics study of the STEP61 interactome. Here, we explored the relationship between STEP61 and mGluR5 in greater detail and find that STEP61, like mGluR5, is preferentially localized to extra-synaptic sites in neurons using electron microscopy. A systematic evaluation of STEP61 in heterologous cells identifies its kinase-interacting and amino-terminal domains as being important for mGluR5 binding. Interestingly, we find that STEP61 decreases mGluR5 surface and total protein levels in both heterologous cells and neurons in a lysosome-dependent manner. Conversely, mGluR5 protein and tyrosine phosphorylation levels are increased in STEP knockout (KO) mouse brain. There are four tyrosine residues in the cytosolic tail region of mGluR5, and their mutation decreases total and surface receptor protein levels. Together, these findings reveal an important role of STEP61-mediated tyrosine dephosphorylation as a negative regulator of mGluR5 surface protein levels and stability.

secondary.title: MERTK-related engulfment of norepinephrinergic neuronal presynaptic membrane by astrocytes following acute TBI and potentiation effect of peripheral nerve modulation.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The study investigated the locus coeruleus (LC) changes after acute traumatic brain injury (TBI) and the effects of peripheral nerve modulation (PNM) in a mouse model. METHODS: We performed closed controlled impact to simulate TBI in mice. We adopted electrical stimulation of the right median nerve as a method of PNM. Low-frequency and high-frequency peripheral nerve modulation (LF-PNM and HF-PNM) were administered on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd days after the injury. We conducted a cell interaction analysis on the single-cell data of the mouse brainstem from the previous stage. Meanwhile, we also performed arousal and stress behavioral tests, immunofluorescence staining for apoptosis and activation of LC norepinephrinergic neurons, and examination of astrocytic phagocytosis in association with MERTK expression. RESULTS: Acute TBI induced apoptosis of LC norepinephrinergic neurons alongside behavioral impairments. TBI triggered reactive astrogliosis in the LC, with elevated GFAP-Lamp2 colocalization. Increased GFAP-NET colocalization indicated astrocytic engulfment of presynaptic membrane proteins from norepinephrinergic neurons. Cell interaction analysis identified MERTK-mediated astrocyte-norepinephrinergic neuron crosstalk; GFAP-MERTK immunofluorescence confirmed spatially increased astrocytic MERTK expression linked to NET phagocytosis. LF-PNM further enhanced astrocytic phagocytosis of LC norepinephrinergic presynaptic proteins after TBI, reduced neuronal apoptosis, facilitated neuronal activation, and rescued arousal and stress functions. CONCLUSION: After acute TBI, LC astrocytes phagocytose norepinephrinergic presynaptic proteins via MERTK. LF-PNM enhances this process, improving post-TBI arousal and stress dysfunction.

secondary.title: Elevated miR-103b in exosomes derived from brain-metastatic triple-negative breast cancer cells remodels the brain pre-metastatic niche (PMN).
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive breast cancer with high brain metastatic (BM) potential. Tumor-derived exosomes are implicated as key modulators during the formation of the pre-metastatic niche (PMN). However, the regulation of TNBC-BM-derived exosomes on brain PMN remains enigmatic. METHODS: The morphology and uptake of exosomes were identified using transmission electron microscopy and live-cell imaging, respectively. Differentially secreted miRNAs and mRNA were identified using high-throughput sequencing. The permeability of the blood‒brain barrier (BBB) and tight junction integrity were examined using immunofluorescence staining. Cell viability was examined using the CCK-8 assay. The apoptosis and intracellular ROS were investigated using fluorescence staining. The expression of mRNAs was examined using qPCR. RESULTS: miR-103b was significantly increased in exosomes derived from TNBC-BM cells. miR-103b compromised the tight junctions of HUVECs and increased BBB permeability in mice. Additionally, miR-103b promoted apoptosis and increased intracellular ROS in HUVECs and U251 cells, two cell lines commonly used as surrogates for brain microvascular endothelial cells and astrocytes, respectively. miR-103b-regulated differentially expressed genes modulated tight junction, apoptosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and metabolism. Target analysis identified 216 targets of miR-103b, among which hub targets were associated with biological processes involved in maintaining the BBB and the glucose metabolism signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings for the first time reveal that exosomal miR-103b from TNBC-BM cells potentially regulates the two major cellular constituents of the brain PMN, highlighting its role in the formation of the brain PMN during TNBC-BM and its potential as a promising therapeutic target.

secondary.title: Mapping the knowledge structure and emerging trends of blood-based biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: A bibliometric analysis (2016-2026).
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, and its diagnosis still relies mainly on behavioral assessment. Blood-based biomarkers may provide objective support for early detection, biological subgrouping, clinical monitoring, and individualized intervention. However, findings in this field remain dispersed across multiple biological pathways. This study aimed to map the knowledge structure and emerging trends of ASD blood-based biomarker research. METHODS: Publications on ASD blood-based biomarkers from 2016 to 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. After duplicate removal and eligibility screening, 1785 English-language articles and reviews were included. CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Microsoft Excel were used to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, influential journals and authors, co-cited references, keyword clusters, and citation bursts. RESULTS: Research output increased steadily, with the United States and China contributing the largest number of publications and the United States showing stronger international connectivity. Co-cited reference and keyword analyses identified oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, gut microbiota, metabolomics, mitochondrial respiration, and gastrointestinal symptoms as major knowledge clusters. Recent burst terms, including machine learning, Mendelian randomization, gut-brain axis, innate immunity, sex differences, and neurological disorders, indicate a shift toward causal inference, multi-omics integration, and data-driven biomarker prediction. CONCLUSIONS: ASD blood-based biomarker research has grown steadily over the past decade and is moving from descriptive clinical observations toward mechanistic, multi-omics, and computational approaches. Oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, gut-brain interactions, inflammatory responses, and machine learning-based prediction now represent major directions in this field. Future studies should focus on multicenter longitudinal cohorts, standardized analytical workflows, detailed clinical phenotyping, and independent validation to improve reproducibility and support clinical translation.

secondary.title: Application of digital pathology to assess the effect of hormone treatment on placental histomorphometry in mares with induced ascending placentitis.
secondary.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of hormonal treatments with altrenogest (ALT) and estradiol cypionate (ECP) on placental histomorphometry in mares with experimentally induced ascending placentitis, using digital pathology as a quantitative tool. Thirty pregnancies from 27 Criollo-type mares were assigned to six groups: healthy controls (n = 5); basic treatment (n = 5), treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TSM), and flunixin meglumine (FM); ALT group (n = 5) + basic treatment; ECP group (n = 5) + basic treatment; ALT + ECP group (n = 5) in addition to basic treatment; and an untreated placentitis group (n = 5). Following parturition, chorioallantoic samples were collected from the cervical star, uterine body, and both horns. Digital images were analyzed using NIH ImageJ software to quantify microcotyledonary and capillary areas per field. Gestation length in the ECP group was comparable to that of the healthy controls, while placental weight and expulsion time did not differ significantly among groups. Histomorphometric analysis revealed that mares in the ECP group exhibited significantly increased capillary area and total microcotyledonary area compared to other placentitis groups. These results suggest that ECP enhances placental vascularization and microstructure in mares with ascending placentitis. The findings support the therapeutic potential of ECP in promoting placental recovery and maintaining uterine homeostasis. Additionally, this study highlights the utility of digital pathology in the quantitative assessment of equine placental morphology, providing new perspectives for improving therapeutic strategies in the management of placentitis.

secondary.title: A reproducible entropy-weighted Gower-CLARA-TOPSIS procedure for mixed-type MSME segmentation and prioritization.
secondary.abstract: In this paper a reproducible approach for segmentation of mixed-type data and the within-cluster prioritizing is presented. The procedure keeps raw categorical values for Gower dissimilarity, binary or count representations only for entropy weighting, applies CLARA to repeated samples with PAM medoids, and evaluates weighted and Top-N feature configurations with the Silhouette Coefficient, medoid-based Davies-Bouldin Index, and Calinski-Harabasz Index. The chosen configuration is then utilized to rank within clusters, instead of between clusters using TOPSIS to evaluate the economic-operational preparedness of similar firms. It presents a worked example with 1049 de-duplicated MSME records from Sampang, Indonesia, with numerical, binary, count and categorical attributes. The optimum configuration selected four operational and financial aspects and increased the Silhouette Coefficient from 0.4183 to 0.5588, decreased the Davies-Bouldin Index from 1.2393 to 0.6181, and boosted the Calinski-Harabasz Index from 357.7787 to 992.3958. By combining entropy-based feature weighting, weighted Gower dissimilarity, CLARA sampling, and Top-N feature selection, the procedure provides transparent mixed-data segmentation while preserving categorical semantics and separating clustering from peer-group-based TOPSIS ranking. A reference Jupyter Notebook implementation and an anonymized or de-identified demonstration dataset are supplied to support inspection and reuse of the workflow.

secondary.title: Semantic-Aware Semi-Supervised Systematic Segmentation for Brain Magnetic Resonance Image.
secondary.abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain MRI images is essential for early diagnosis and prevention of brain tumors and strokes. However, it is challenging due to data scarcity, domain shift, complexity, and blurred edges. Recent methods use mean-teacher model learning for the semantic details of an individual image based on the efficiency of teacher architecture. However, to enhance the segmentation in brain MRI, the paper introduces SemS4, a semi-supervised method on the basis of cross-image architecture. SemS4 uses a single architecture integrating an Edge Prototype Attention (EPA) and a foreground prototype attention (FPA). More specifically, EPA uses edge prototype integrated with adaptive edge container to improve the edge features for which global edge features are stored to produce edge prototype. Moreover, FPA stabilizes the segmentation by transferring complementary foreground information. Furthermore, the proposed method uses Pixel Affinity Loss (PAL) for missing contextual correlation during supervision to enhance segmentation performance on edges. The performance of the proposed approach in experimental results for two brain MRI benchmarks, LGG and BRISC, validates the superiority over existing methods under different partitioning settings.

secondary.title: RV-mixer: Random Fourier and variance-guided global feature learning for medical image segmentation.
secondary.abstract: Hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures have achieved promising performance in medical image segmentation, yet the high computational cost of self-attention limits their application in resource-constrained clinical scenarios. Moreover, medical images exhibit domain-specific challenges, including ultrasound speckle noise, low contrast, and ambiguous lesion boundaries, which require robust feature representation beyond conventional local modeling. To address these issues, we propose RV-Mixer, a lightweight module for efficient global representation learning with medical-domain priors. Instead of explicit attention-based token interaction, RV-Mixer employs Random Fourier Features (RFF) to project local representations into a shared frequency-domain embedding space, providing nonlinear feature enhancement with low computational overhead. Furthermore, Variance-Guided Channel Recalibration (VGCR) introduces global statistical aggregation through channel-wise variance modeling, enabling adaptive emphasis of discriminative pathological textures and lesion boundaries that may be weakened by mean-based feature aggregation. Extensive experiments on five public medical image segmentation datasets, covering ultrasound, endoscopy, dermoscopy, and MRI scenarios, demonstrate that RV-Mixer achieves competitive or superior performance compared with Transformer-, MLP-, and Mamba-based approaches while maintaining fewer parameters and lower computational complexity. These results highlight the effectiveness of domain-informed frequency representation and statistical global aggregation for efficient and robust medical image segmentation.

primary.title: cAMP signaling promotes acute lysosome biogenesis through TFEB nuclear import-export dynamics.
primary.abstract: Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling is a major stimulus for lipid and glucose catabolism, yet catabolic processes like these can also coordinate with lysosome-dependent degradation. However, the impact of cAMP signaling on lysosomal dynamics remains unclear. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, is regulated by stimulus-dependent nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling through a variety of phosphorylation events. Here, we find that elevating intracellular cAMP with forskolin and IBMX induces rapid nuclear import of TFEB-GFP within 30 minutes and coincides with a transient upregulation of TFEB target lysosome genes. By 8 hours, TFEB returns to the cytoplasm, accompanied by transcriptional downregulation. Inhibition of cAMP-dependent protein kinase A (PKA) using H89 did not block nuclear import but unexpectedly caused sustained nuclear accumulation, indicating that PKA promotes TFEB nuclear export. Consistent with this, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed increased phosphorylation of a PKA-consensus motif (RRxS) during the export phase. These findings suggest that cAMP-PKA signaling plays a novel role in temporally "tuning" lysosomal gene expression by regulating TFEB nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling.

primary.title: TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 links bacteria recognition to autophagosome formation in xenophagy.
primary.abstract: Xenophagy, a selective autophagy pathway, is a critical innate immune defense mechanism that targets pathogens for lysosomal degradation. However, the molecular mechanisms enabling autophagosomes to specifically recognize and engulf bacteria remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify WIPI2, a core component that drives autophagosome biogenesis, as a novel phosphorylation substrate of TBK1 during Salmonella Typhimurium infection. We demonstrate that TBK1 phosphorylates WIPI2 at Ser96, which enhances its interaction with ATG16L1 and its binding to PtdIns3P. Crucially, the recruitment of WIPI2 to intracellular bacteria is dependent on its interaction with ATG16L1, which is localized to the Salmonella-containing vacuole. Furthermore, TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 is required for efficient bacterial clearance. Collectively, our findings reveal a molecular mechanism whereby TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 directs localized phagophore expansion around invading bacteria, thereby bridging bacterial recognition with autophagosome assembly.Abbreviations: ATG: autophagy related; ATG5: autophagy related 5; ATG16L1: autophagy related 16 like 1; CALCOCO2/NDP52: calcium binding and coiled-coil domain 2; CFU: colony-forming units; GFP: green fluorescent protein; GST: glutathione S-transferase; IL6: interleukin 6; KO: knockout; LPS: lipopolysaccharides; MAP1LC3/LC3: microtubule associated protein 1 light chain 3; OPTN: optineurin; PtdIns: phosphatidylinositol; PtdIns3P: phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate; RB1CC1/FIP200: RB1 inducible coiled-coil 1; RFP: red fluorescent protein;S. primary.title: Tet1-mediated 5-hydroxymethylcytosine alterations in the olfactory bulb are associated with aberrant neurogenesis and PI3K-Akt signaling in response to CIH.
primary.abstract: Chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH), a key feature of obstructive sleep apnea, impairs central nervous system function, but its effects on olfactory bulb (OB) and epigenetic mechanisms are unclear. We show that CIH causes olfactory behavioral deficits in mice with structural and molecular OB changes. CIH disrupted adult OB neurogenesis, increasing the immature neuron marker doublecortin (DCX) and reducing mature NeuN expression, and activated microglia. At the molecular level, CIH markedly upregulated the DNA demethylation enzyme Tet1 and global 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) levels, which were accompanied by aberrant activation of the PI3K-Akt pathway. Importantly, Tet1 knockdown in the OB partially normalized PI3K-Akt signaling, was associated with improved neurogenesis markers, and alleviated CIH-induced olfactory dysfunction. These results suggest that Tet1-dependent epigenetic remodeling represents an important molecular mechanism linking CIH to OB dysfunction, and that Tet1 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for CIH-related sensory impairment.

primary.title: Astrocytic TRPC6 protects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by inhibiting cGAS-STING pathway.
primary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is complicated by BBB breakdown and neuroinflammation, processes partially regulated by astrocytes. This study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective mechanism of astrocyte-specific TRPC6, focusing on elucidating its molecular link to the cGAS-STING pathway and BBB integrity. METHODS: MCAO mouse models were established, with astrocyte-specific TRPC6 overexpression achieved via stereotactic injection of AAV-GFAP-Trpc6. Neurological function, infarct volume, apoptosis, and BBB integrity (including tight junction proteins and AQP4) were systematically assessed. In vitro, OGD/R conditioned medium culture and co-culture were used for mechanistic validation, with the STING agonist ADU-S100 employed for intervention and causality confirmation. RESULTS: Astrocyte TRPC6 overexpression significantly improved neurological function and behavioral outcomes, reduced infarct volume, and inhibited neuronal apoptosis. TRPC6 overexpression also stabilized the BBB, shown by reduced cerebral edema, reversed tight junction protein (ZO-1/Occludin) loss, and decreased AQP4 expression. Mechanistic analysis confirmed that TRPC6 overexpression significantly suppressed CIRI-induced activation of the astrocytic cGAS-STING pathway. The STING agonist ADU-S100 partially reversed the neuroprotective and BBB-stabilizing effects of TRPC6. CONCLUSION: Astrocytic TRPC6 maintains BBB integrity by negatively regulating the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway in the early phase of CIRI. The study identified the "Astrocyte TRPC6-STING-Tight Junction" axis, offering a precise and promising novel therapeutic target for CIRI.

secondary.title: Essential Oils From the Fruit of Amomum villosum Lour. Alleviate LPS-Induced Neuroinflammation by Repressing PI3K-Akt and MAPK Signaling Pathways.
secondary.abstract: Amomum villosum Lour. has been traditionally valued in various cultures for its health benefits. Here, we show that the neuroprotective effects of the essential oils extracted from the fruit of Amomum villosum Lour. (AVEO) and elucidate its underlying mechanisms in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammation. The main compounds of AVEO can cross the blood-brain barrier and significantly improve cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in LPS-induced mice, leading to a 50% enhancement in Morris water maze performance, a 60% and 80% reduction in immobility time in the tail suspension test and forced swimming test, respectively. Moreover, AVEO mitigates neuron loss and suppresses the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators, including TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, while upregulating the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 in brain tissue. RNA-seq and metabonomics analyses reveal that AVEO modulates multiple inflammation-related pathways and restore metabolic homeostasis in brain tissue. Remarkably, AVEO attenuates hyperactivation of the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways in LPS-induced microglia and improves neuronal damage in LPS-induced microglia-neuron co-culture system. Altogether, our findings suggest that AVEO alleviates neural dysfunction by modulating PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling cascades and promoting metabolic reprogramming upon neuroinflammation, thereby revealing the therapeutic potential of AVEO in several neurological disorders.

secondary.title: Targeting the Calcium-mtDNA-cGAS-STING Signaling Nexus: A Novel Redox Mechanism for Nimodipine's Neuroprotection in Traumatic Brain Injury.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) induces severe secondary injury where molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates the involvement of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) signaling pathway in this process and evaluates the neuroprotective effect of the L-type calcium channel blocker nimodipine, focusing on calcium homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and inflammatory signaling. METHODS: Using primary neuronal and mouse TBI models, we assessed outcomes via fluorescent calcium imaging, JC-1 staining, Western blot, quantitative PCR (qPCR)/reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and behavioral tests. Nimodipine was applied to inhibit L-type channels, specifically testing its role in reducing mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release, blocking cGAS-STING activation, and suppressing neuroinflammation. RESULTS: TBI markedly activated the cGAS-STING pathway, increasing pro-inflammatory factors and apoptosis. In the cellular oxygen-glucose deprivation model, calcium overload was directly observed by Fluo-4 AM staining and was associated with subsequent mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening and mtDNA release, identifying this process as a key upstream event for cGAS-STING activation. Nimodipine inhibited intracellular calcium overload, reduced mitochondrial injury and mtDNA release, and consequently suppressed cGAS-STING pathway activation. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments showed dose-dependent decreases in pro-inflammatory factors, along with improved neurological function and attenuated brain tissue pathology. CONCLUSION: Nimodipine attenuates secondary neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis after TBI by inhibiting calcium influx, decreasing mtDNA release, and suppressing cGAS-STING signaling. These results suggest that the Ca2+-mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis contributes to TBI pathology and that nimodipine may serve as a potential multitarget therapy. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

secondary.title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation.
secondary.abstract: Preoperative sleep deprivation (SD) is known to exacerbate postoperative pain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using a male mouse model of 48-hour continuous SD followed by incisional surgery, we found that SD alone induced transient mechanical hyperalgesia, and when combined with surgery (SI group) it significantly aggravated and prolonged postoperative pain recovery until day 10. On postoperative day 7, SI mice showed marked downregulation of spinal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression and decreased spinal dopamine concentration. D2R was predominantly expressed on spinal glutamatergic neurons. Overexpression of D2R on these neurons via intrathecal AAV injection effectively alleviated the prolonged hyperalgesia, normalizing pain sensitivity by day 7. Mechanistically, D2R downregulation led to increased phosphorylation of NMDA receptor subunits (p-NR1 and p-NR2B) without altering total NMDA receptor levels. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between D2R and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). SI mice exhibited decreased PP2A expression but increased p-AKT, p-GSK3β, and β-catenin, indicating activation of the PP2A/AKT signaling pathway, which were reversed by D2R overexpression. Furthermore, pharmacological activation of PP2A with DT-061 not only downregulated p-AKT, p-GSK3β, β-catenin, p-NR1 and p-NR2B, but also produced significant analgesia in SI mice. Collectively, these results demonstrate that preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal D2R on glutamatergic neurons, which disinhibits the PP2A/AKT pathway and enhances NMDA receptor phosphorylation. Targeting D2R or its downstream PP2A/AKT signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for managing persistent postoperative pain caused by preoperative sleep deprivation in male mice.

secondary.title: Six3 promoting the migration and neural differentiation of BMSCs via Btg2‑mediated Akt signaling pathway activation: A therapeutic strategy for stroke.
secondary.abstract: Bone marrow‑derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) transplantation holds therapeutic potential for stroke; however, but its effectiveness requires optimization. The transcription factor Sine Oculis Homeobox Homolog 3 (Six3) regulates processes crucial for BMSC therapy, such as neural cell proliferation and differentiation. However, whether Six3‑modified BMSCs exert enhanced therapeutic effects on stroke remains unknown. In the present study, mouse BMSCs were isolated and identified using surface markers. Six3‑overexpressing BMSCs exhibited enhanced proliferative, migratory and neural differentiation capacities. RNA‑sequencing analysis comparing the gene expression profiles of BMSCs with and without Six3 overexpression identified BTG Anti‑Proliferation Factor 2 (Btg2) as an upregulated gene (log2FC=1.45, P<0.05) in Six3‑overexpressing cells. Further investigations revealed that Six3 directly binds to the TGATACTGTCT sequence within the Btg2 promoter and activates its transcription. Btg2 knockdown abolished the effects of Six3 overexpression. Mechanistically, Six3 promoted Akt phosphorylation via Btg2, enhancing BMSC viability and neural differentiation. A mouse model of stroke was established using transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO, 1.5‑h occlusion and 24‑h reperfusion). BMSCs were administered via tail vein injection at the onset of reperfusion. GFP expression detected in brain tissue at 24 h post‑reperfusion confirmed successful the homing of BMSCs to the brain. The transplantation of Six3‑overexpressing BMSCs ameliorated brain pathology, reducing apoptosis and cerebral infarct volume. Notably, Six3‑modified BMSCs demonstrated a significantly greater therapeutic efficacy than unmodified BMSCs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Six3 enhances the therapeutic properties of BMSCs by transcriptionally activating Btg2, which promotes Akt phosphorylation. These findings provide novel mechanistic insight into the optimization of stem cell therapy in stroke.

secondary.title: PDE2A is involved in negative emotional behaviors via the cAMP-PKA signaling pathway in the SPS&S model.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by negative affective symptoms, including anxiety, depression, anhedonia, and fear. The molecular mechanisms underlying these symptoms remain poorly understood. Phosphodiesterase 2A (PDE2A), a regulator of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling, has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the role of the PDE2A-cAMP-protein kinase A (PKA) signaling pathway in negative emotional behaviors induced by traumatic stress. METHODS: Transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. A rat PTSD model was established using single prolonged stress combined with foot shocks (SPS&S). Behavioral tests were performed, and PDE2A-cAMP-PKA signaling alterations in the amygdala were examined. The effects of PDE2A inhibitor Hcyb1 and the PKA inhibitor H89 were evaluated. RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified PDE2A as a hub gene associated with PTSD, with significant enrichment of the cAMP signaling pathway. SPS&S rats exhibited anxiety-, depression-like behaviors, and anhedonia, accompanied by increased PDE2A expression and reduced cAMP and phosphorylated PKA (p-PKA) levels in the amygdala. Hcyb1 treatment alleviated behavioral deficits, decreased PDE2A expression, and restored cAMP and p-PKA signaling. H89 blocked p-PKA activation and partially reversed the behavioral benefits of Hcyb1. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that amygdala PDE2A-cAMP-PKA signaling is associated with negative emotional behaviors in the SPS&S model. PDE2A inhibition may ameliorate behavioral deficits through PKA-related signaling. However, the peripheral blood transcriptomic data, lack of direct PDE2A activity and cAMP/cGMP measurements, and limited biochemical validation constrain mechanistic interpretation. Further studies using brain-derived datasets and comprehensive biochemical approaches are warranted.

secondary.title: Stigmasterol alleviates central precocious puberty by targeting the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway and modulating the Kisspeptin/GnRH axis.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Central precocious puberty (CPP) results from premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, causing early sexual development and related health risks. Stigmasterol (ST), a natural phytosterol with diverse pharmacological activities, has not been fully evaluated for CPP. METHODS: This study integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify ST targets in CPP. Experimental validation used an N-Methyl aspartic acid-induced CPP rat model and high-glucose high-fat-stimulated GT1-7 hypothalamic neurons. Techniques included histology, ELISA, qPCR, western blot, and flow cytometry. RESULTS: In silico analyses demonstrated favorable binding of ST to core proteins within the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway. In vivo, ST treatment significantly delayed vaginal opening, reduced serum levels of estradiol and testosterone, and ameliorated pathological abnormalities in uterine and ovarian tissues. At the molecular level, ST suppressed the hypothalamic overactivation of the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway and attenuated neuronal damage and apoptosis. In vitro, ST inhibited HGHF-induced proliferation, inflammatory cytokine release, and apoptosis in GT1-7 cells, while concurrently modulating the expression of key puberty-related genes and proteins, including those within the Kisspeptin/GnRH axis. Conversely, pharmacological reactivation of PI3K signaling with the agonist 740YP attenuated selected protective effects the protective effects of ST, supporting the functional involvement the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway in mediating these benefits. CONCLUSIONS: Stigmasterol exhibits significant therapeutic effects against CPP by concurrently targeting the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR and Kisspeptin/GnRH signaling pathways. These findings provide robust preclinical evidence supporting ST as a promising multi-targeted natural candidate for CPP management.

secondary.title: Insulin regulates activity-dependent mitochondrial depolarization and calcium dynamics in dentate granule cells.
secondary.abstract: Systemic insulin resistance is associated with reduced hippocampal energy metabolism and cognitive impairment both in humans and animal models. However, whether insulin rapidly regulates neuronal metabolic stability during activity remains unclear. Here, we examined insulin signaling and queried the corresponding mitochondrial responses in dentate granule cells (DGCs) of adult female mice. This layer of excitatory neurons within the hippocampus plays an essential role in learning and memory. Insulin robustly increased Akt phosphorylation in dentate gyrus tissue when insulin degradation was inhibited, and this response was attenuated by genetic deletion of the insulin receptor in DGCs, consistent with cell-autonomous signaling. We found that insulin did not alter mitochondrial membrane potential at rest, but significantly limited activity-evoked mitochondrial depolarization induced by neuronal stimulation. However, this change had no measurable impact on cytosolic ATP availability and was instead associated with Ca2+ dynamics. Removing Ca2+ ions from the extracellular solution, or disrupting mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake, prevented insulin modulation of the mitochondrial membrane potential. Furthermore, insulin limited cytosolic Ca2+ accumulation through an insulin receptor-dependent mechanism that persisted despite Akt inhibition. Insulin also accelerated the clearance of mitochondrial Ca2+ transients in active neurons, which occurred without changes in either neuronal excitability or pyruvate dehydrogenase phosphorylation. Together, these findings identify endogenous insulin degradation as a key regulator of hippocampal insulin signaling, and reveal a previously unrecognized interaction between insulin and Ca2+ signaling in stimulated DGCs. This work also establishes a direct link between central insulin signaling and the maintenance of mitochondrial electrochemical homeostasis in the adult brain.Significance Statement Insulin signaling is known to influence synaptic plasticity, yet its direct effects on neuronal metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we show that endogenous insulin degradation limits insulin signaling in adult hippocampal tissue. This finding suggests that inhibitors of the insulin degrading enzyme may hold the potential to improve the efficacy of insulin-based interventions aimed at improving learning and memory. Acute insulin signaling does not modify neuronal excitability, or cytosolic ATP availability. Instead, it stabilizes mitochondrial membrane potential and reduces calcium accumulation in active dentate granule cells. By identifying an insulin-dependent mechanism that regulates the electrochemical homeostasis of mitochondria in active neurons, this work provides insight into how brain insulin resistance may contribute to cognitive dysfunction in aging and neurometabolic disorders.

secondary.title: Molecular Signatures of HIV-Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV.
secondary.abstract: HIV-associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV-related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV-1-infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three-dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected, cART-treated rhesus macaque model. Integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing with ATAC-seq (multi-omics), identifies cell-type-specific alterations in dual innate immune-driven inflammatory signaling pathways across neural and glial populations in hCOs. Microglia were preferentially infected and activated, initiating IL-17A-mediated cascades involving IFN-γ/STAT1, CEBPB, and NF-κB signaling. These pathways converged with cGAS-STING and Notch-NEURL1 signaling, both associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction. cART suppressed viral replication, reduced IL-17A-mediated neuroinflammation, improved mitochondrial function, and restored synaptic gene expression. Collectively, these findings identify dysregulation of IL-17A, STAT1, CEBPB, and cGAS-STING signaling as key molecular drivers of HIV-associated neuroinflammation. They also establish a potential mechanistic link between IL-17A signaling and microglial remodeling, providing a translational framework for the development of CNS-targeted therapies in PWH.

secondary.title: YBX3 promotes ischemia-reperfusion injury by enhancing microglial glycolysis via PKM2 stabilization and mTOR-HIF-1α pathway activation.
secondary.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation and metabolic dysfunction playing central roles in its pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated the function of Y-box binding protein 3 (YBX3) in ischemic stroke, with particular focus on its regulation of glycolysis and neuroinflammatory responses. Using a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in C57BL/6 mice and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model in BV2 microglia, we observed that YBX3 expression was markedly upregulated following ischemia-reperfusion. Overexpression of YBX3 aggravated cerebral infarct size, worsened motor and neurological outcomes, and increased the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) both in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, YBX3 enhanced glycolysis in BV2 cells by stabilizing pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) mRNA and promoting its expression, while simultaneously activating glycolysis through the mTOR-HIF-1α signaling pathway. Pharmacological inhibition of mTOR with rapamycin reversed YBX3-induced glycolytic activation, neuroinflammation, and neuronal injury. Collectively, these results identify YBX3 as a key regulator of ischemic brain damage through glycolysis-dependent mechanisms and underscore its potential as a therapeutic target for stroke.

secondary.title: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles induce neurotoxicity through PI3K/Akt-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis.
secondary.abstract: Concerns about chronic exposure to titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO2-NPs) have increased because of their widespread use in consumer products and subsequent environmental release. Previous studies have shown that TiO2-NPs exert neurotoxic effects and may contribute to Parkinson's disease (PD)-related neurodegenerative processes. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying TiO2-NPs-induced neurotoxicity remain unclear. We investigated these effects and their potential mechanisms in A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice and SH-SY5Y cells. Repeated oral exposure to TiO2-NPs for two months dose-dependently aggravated motor dysfunction and neuronal degeneration in the substantia nigra pars compacta at 1, 10, and 50 mg/kg body weight. In SH‑SY5Y cells, exposure to TiO2‑NPs for 48 h at 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 50, and 100 mg/L reduced cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner, impaired mitochondrial function, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and promoted apoptosis. Western blotting showed that TiO2-NPs inhibited PI3K/Akt signaling and altered mitochondrial apoptosis-related proteins, including Bcl-2, Bax, cytochrome C (Cyt C) and caspase-3. The PI3K agonist insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) partly attenuated these changes. These findings provide mechanistic evidence for TiO2-NPs-induced neurotoxicity and may support the health risk assessment and safe application of TiO2-NPs.

secondary.title: Investigating the role of norepinephrine in regulating depression by a novel organic near-infrared fluorescent probe.
secondary.abstract: Depression is closely associated with alterations in concentration levels and release dynamics of a specific neurotransmitter, such as norepinephrine (NE), in the brain. Visualizing these dynamic changes is essential for understanding depression-associated neurotransmitter dysregulation. Herein, we developed a novel near-infrared fluorescent probe DIPCl-NE by employing a near-infrared fluorophore DIPCl-OH (Em = 689 nm) as the signal reporter and introducing a carbonothioate group as the recognition unit for selective NE detection. DIPCl-NE exhibits high sensitivity, excellent selectivity, good photostability, and effective tissue penetration capability. Using this probe, we visualized NE release dynamics in normal and CORT-induced depressive-like models and revealed that impaired NE exocytosis is associated with reduced mTOR phosphorylation levels. Pharmacological regulation of mTOR signaling further demonstrated its role in modulating NE release dynamics. Moreover, DIPCl-NE enabled visualization of NE alterations in mouse brains and revealed decreased NE availability in depressive model mice. This work provides a valuable chemical tool for monitoring NE dynamics and offers new insights into the relationship between mTOR signaling and depression-associated neurotransmitter dysfunction.

secondary.title: APOE4-AGE axis is linked to mtDNA release and cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammation in the aging brain.
secondary.abstract: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) accumulate with aging and have been implicated in neurodegeneration, yet their relationship with the APOE4 genotype and downstream inflammatory signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we show that APOE4 is associated with greater age-dependent AGE accumulation and APOE glycation in the aging brain compared with APOE3 in animal models. These changes are accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction and increased release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) into the cytosol, providing a potential trigger for innate immune activation. Consistent with enhanced innate immune signaling, APOE4 brains exhibit increased cGAS expression and phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3, together with elevated type I interferon and pro-inflammatory responses. This activation is particularly prominent in microglia, as demonstrated by increased cGAS-DNA interactions and greater colocalization of cGAS signaling with Iba1-positive cells. APOE4 mice further display increased levels of cGAMP and IFN-β, as well as enhanced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and interferon-stimulated genes. Mechanistically, exposure of primary microglia to AGEs induces cytosolic mtDNA release and activates cGAS-STING signaling, whereas pharmacological inhibition of the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) attenuates these responses. Together, these findings identify an association between the APOE4-AGE axis, mitochondrial dysfunction, mtDNA release, and enhanced cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling in the aging brain, while the in vitro studies support a functional contribution of AGE-RAGE signaling to these responses in primary microglia.

secondary.title: Activation of mTOR pathway by human cytomegalovirus promoting host ribosomal protein expression by coordinated transcriptional and translational controls.
secondary.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) profoundly reprograms host transcription and RNA metabolism, yet its impact on transcription start site (TSS) regulation of host genes remains poorly understood. Here, we employed NanoCap Analysis of Gene Expression sequencing (NanoCAGE-seq) to investigate HCMV-driven changes in alternative TSS usage across the host transcriptome. We identified widespread TSS switching, with ribosomal protein genes (RPGs) emerging as a highly enriched category. Alternative TSS usage produced isoforms with distinct 5'untranslated regions (UTRs), thereby altering cis-regulatory elements that shape translational efficiency. Integrative transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed a paradoxical accumulation of RPG proteins despite transcriptional downregulation during infection. Using 5' Rapid Amplification of cDNA Ends (5'RACE), we characterized four RPGs of RPL4, RPS11, RPS23, and RPS24 that generated 5'UTR variants through alternative TSS usage. Notably, isoforms containing a 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif were significantly enriched, correlating with mTOR activation induced by HCMV. Functional assays with bicistronic reporter constructs in HEK293 cells and infection models in human embryonic lung fibroblasts demonstrated that the RPL4 5'TOP isoform exhibited enhanced mTORC1-driven translation compared with non-5'TOP counterparts. Importantly, RPL4 upregulation facilitated viral protein synthesis and boosted production of infectious virions. Together, our findings reveal that dynamic TSS switching of RPGs provides a simple, yet effective, mechanism for fine-tuning mTORC1-responsive translation. By co-opting host transcriptional and translational programs, HCMV enhances ribosome function to optimize the cellular environment for productive viral replication.

secondary.title: Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCU-41 reduces oxidative stress to ameliorate Parkinson's disease by regulating the AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
secondary.abstract: A growing body of evidence suggests that the gut microbiota influences the onset and progression of Parkinson's disease (PD) by regulating oxidative stress pathways. However, existing evidence remains the phenotypic level, and high-quality research is still lacking regarding specific probiotic strains with clearly defined ameliorative functions and their precise underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, high-throughput sequencing confirmed significant differences in the gut microbiota between PD patients and healthy individuals. Furthermore, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy individuals significantly improved motor dysfunction in PD mice, reduced α-syn aggregation (MP vs. M = 319.61 ng/ML vs. 507.84 ng/ML), alleviated neuroinflammation (reduced GFAP and IBA1 positive areas), protected dopaminergic neurons (increased TH expression), and optimized the structure of the gut microbiota, whereas FMT from PD patients exacerbated PD progression. Additionally, through correlation analysis, culturomics, and tryptophan metabolite analysis, Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCU-41 may improve PD by producing indole-3-lactic acid (ILA). Further validation through animal experiments demonstrating that supplementation with either NCU-41 or ILA alone significantly improved PD symptoms, though not as effectively as FMT from healthy individuals. Mechanistically, NCU-41 might activate the AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway through its tryptophan metabolite (ILA), thereby enhancing the body's antioxidant capacity and ultimately alleviating PD. In summary, this study revealed that L. salivarius NCU-41 to activate the AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway, thereby exerting a therapeutic effect on PD. These findings provide a deeper mechanistic basis for the potential application of this strain in the future treatment of PD.

secondary.title: Neuroprotective effects of chitosan nanoparticle-loaded orientin in a 6-OHDA-induced Parkinson's disease experimental model in rats.
secondary.abstract: PURPOSE: The present study investigated the neuroprotective effects of orientin, a natural flavonoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, loaded into chitosan nanoparticles (CNPs-Orientin) in a unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-induced rat model of Parkinson's disease. The study further evaluated behavioral performance, histopathological alterations, tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) immunoreactivity, oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, and apoptosis- and survival-related signaling proteins. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seventy-two male Sprague-Dawley rats (220-260 g) were randomly assigned into nine experimental groups (n = 8/group): Control, Orientin, CNPs, CNPs-Orientin, 6-OHDA, 6-OHDA + L-DOPA, 6-OHDA + Orientin, 6-OHDA + CNPs, and 6-OHDA + CNPs-Orientin. Parkinsonism was induced by unilateral stereotaxic injection of 6-OHDA into the substantia nigra pars compacta. Drug treatments were initiated after lesion induction and continued for 14 consecutive days. Behavioral, histopathological, immunohistochemical, biochemical, and Western blot analyses were subsequently performed. RESULTS: 6-OHDA administration caused marked motor impairment, neuronal degeneration, reduced TH immunoreactivity, increased α-synuclein and Beclin-1 immunoreactivity, increased oxidative stress, elevated inflammatory cytokines, increased apoptosis-related protein expression, and suppression of antioxidant defense mechanisms. Treatment with CNPs-Orientin significantly improved behavioral performance, preserved TH-positive neurons, reduced α-synuclein-positive cell density and Beclin-1-positive DAB area, reduced neuronal degeneration, decreased MDA, TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-γ, NF-κB, and Caspase-3 levels, while restoring SOD, GSH, Bcl-2, PI3K, Akt, and mTOR protein expression. Overall, CNPs-Orientin produced greater neuroprotective effects than free orientin alone. CONCLUSION: Chitosan nanoparticle-mediated delivery substantially enhanced the neuroprotective efficacy of the natural flavonoid orientin against 6-OHDA-induced dopaminergic neurodegeneration. The observed protective effects were associated with reduced oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and changes in PI3K/Akt/mTOR-related protein expression.
